plot: Odo and Mothwick follow the true story of the SS Baychimo (Alaska, 1931): ice traps the fur steamer, a blizzard takes her and the crew thinks she sank, but she keeps reappearing empty for 38 years; the twist is the storm freed her as the ice had once before, and the episode ends with a ship's bell ringing on the ice.

script.title: This Ship Escaped Its Crew for 38 Years

beats.say: She's gone! The whole ship is gone! Where is the Baychimo?
A true story. Alaska, November nineteen thirty-one. A ship vanished overnight.
How did a ship with no crew sail on for thirty-eight years?
New episode every day — subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
After that silent snowy camp, I hoped for a quiet night.
Quiet? Odo, we are standing on a frozen sea.
She was a steel steamer, built in Sweden in nineteen fourteen.
The Hudson's Bay Company sent her north each year to trade furs.
On October first, pack ice locked her in, near Barrow, Alaska.
The crew walked to shore. Two days later, she had broken free.
She freed herself! But the ice will grab her again.
It did, a week later. Planes flew twenty-two men out.
Fifteen men stayed behind, in a wooden hut near the ship.
Fifteen men, alone on the ice, guarding one ship.
Then, on November twenty-fourth, a blizzard came howling off the sea.
When the snow stopped, she was gone. Just gone.
Their captain believed she had sunk in the storm.
If she sank, Odo, the furs and the ship are lost forever.
Days later, an Inuit seal hunter arrived with strange news.
I saw your ship. Forty-five miles away. Drifting all alone.
There she was, stuck in the ice again. Empty. Still floating.
Take the best furs! She won't survive another winter.
They carried the most valuable furs off. Then they abandoned her.
So she sank after that... didn't she?
In January nineteen thirty-two, a man crossing by dog sled saw her.
She floated near the shore. Nobody aboard. Nobody at the wheel.
In March nineteen thirty-three, Inuit travellers climbed aboard her.
The storm is too strong! We have to stay inside her!
A sudden storm kept them aboard the empty ship for ten days.
Ten days inside a ship nobody owns. Would you sleep there?
And here is what nobody guessed. That blizzard never sank her.
Just like that first time in October, the storm broke her free.
In August nineteen thirty-three, Scottish traveller Isobel Hutchison went aboard.
Everything is still here, as if the crew might come back.
In nineteen thirty-nine, Captain Hugh Polson came to claim her.
Get a line on her, before the ice starts moving!
Creeping ice floes forced him to give up. She drifted on.
In the forties and fifties, people kept seeing her. Nobody caught her.
In March nineteen sixty-two, Inuit saw her drifting off the Beaufort coast.
In nineteen sixty-nine, she was seen frozen in the pack ice.
Thirty-eight years after her crew walked away. Then, never again.
Never? Not even when people went looking for her?
In two thousand six, Alaska began a search. She is still missing.
Odo, don't move. Listen. Out on the ice... a ship's bell.
Next time: a sealed tomb in Barbados, where the coffins moved.
What do you think happens in the next part? Tell me in the comments.

long.title: This Ship Escaped Its Crew for 38 Years 🚢 (Ep 45)
long.description:
What do you think happens in the next part? Tell me in the comments.

"I thought ships that sink stay sunk. This one never learned." — Odo

A true story: in 1931 ice trapped the fur steamer SS Baychimo off Alaska. After a blizzard her crew believed she had sunk — yet people kept finding her drifting, empty, until 1969.

Sources:

"Creía que los barcos hundidos se quedaban hundidos. Este nunca lo aprendió." — Odo

Una historia real: en 1931 el hielo atrapó al vapor peletero SS Baychimo frente a Alaska. Tras una ventisca, su tripulación lo creyó hundido, pero siguieron viéndolo a la deriva, vacío, hasta 1969.

fr.title: Ce navire a échappé à son équipage 38 ans 🚢 (Ep 45)
fr.description:
Selon vous, que se passe-t-il dans la prochaine partie ? Dites-le-moi en commentaire.

« Je croyais qu'un navire coulé restait au fond. Celui-ci ne l'a jamais compris. » — Odo

Une histoire vraie : en 1931, la glace emprisonne le vapeur de fourrures SS Baychimo au large de l'Alaska. Après un blizzard, l'équipage le croit coulé — pourtant on le revoit dériver, vide, jusqu'en 1969.

de.description:
Was glaubst du, passiert im nächsten Teil? Schreib es mir in die Kommentare.

„Ich dachte, gesunkene Schiffe bleiben unten. Dieses hat es nie gelernt.“ — Odo

Eine wahre Geschichte: 1931 schließt das Eis den Pelzdampfer SS Baychimo vor Alaska ein. Nach einem Schneesturm hält die Crew ihn für gesunken – doch bis 1969 sieht man ihn immer wieder leer treiben.
